A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReSplat with the same authors, core approach, and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original view-synthesis experiments on DL3DV and RealEstate10K, generalization tests, ablations, and reconstructed-scene visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports revised original experiments and additional ACID evaluation, controlled refinement comparisons, architectural ablations, and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the feedback signal from ResNet-feature residuals alone to their sum with projected RGB residuals, using pixel unshuffle, a linear layer, and LayerNorm. This modifies one component while retaining compact initialization, attention-based recurrent updates, and the training losses.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot RealEstate10K-to-ACID evaluation (Table 4) and generalization from eight training views to unseen input-view counts (Figure 5b). Appendix A also evaluates expanded scene coverage with up to 32 views. These substantially broaden the tested generalization scenarios beyond v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SplatFormer (Table 10), 3DGS refinement initialized by ReSplat (Table 8), and depth-regularized 3DGS (Table 11), substantially expanding relevant alternatives. The cited sparse-view optimization papers motivate the depth-regularized comparator; their named methods are not separately reported as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training samples one to four recurrent iterations instead of one to three. New experimental designs control initialization for refinement comparisons, vary weight sharing and network depth, and expand the sampling region and target-view coverage across view counts (Tables 7-9). Existing progressive training schedules and budgets are retained in Appendix B.

E4.justification: v2 expands rendering-error ablations to RGB, feature, and fusion alternatives, and adds coordinate-system, hidden-state, weight-sharing/depth, feature-extractor, and component-runtime analyses (Tables 6, 9, 12, and 13). View-count robustness and qualitative ablations are also added. The original compression and initialization ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional result tables retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported recurrent results change substantially: Table 1's three-iteration PSNR changes from 26.82 to 27.65, with a new four-iteration result of 27.70. Table 2's two-iteration PSNR changes from 23.23 to 23.51, and Table 3 from 29.72 to 29.75. These accompany model/training revisions. ACID, new comparators, and expanded analyses add many results; compression and initialization-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 5 revises the mathematical definition of rendering-error feedback to combine feature residuals with projected RGB residuals. The remaining update and loss mathematics is retained apart from notation and numbering; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain compact Gaussian initialization and gradient-free recurrent refinement. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the generalization claim explicitly to unseen view counts, while the stated empirical scope expands to ACID and 32-view inputs.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism explanations concerning middle-view coordinate alignment, hidden-state features, weight-sharing regularization, and DINOv2's spatial limitations. It also discusses the narrowing advantage over optimization with more views. The limitations retain computational bottlenecks but remove v1's conjecture that fixed Gaussian counts cause iteration saturation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies two-layer Gaussian and four-layer update heads, the middle-view coordinate reference, and details of additional baseline adaptations. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified implementations. Training budgets are relocated unchanged, and code release remains prospective. Table 1 removes the explicit single-GH200 timing-hardware statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for LayerNorm, COLMAP, ACID, and two sparse-view optimization works, and expands its discussion of SplatFormer's scene-level adaptation difficulties. The main related-work organization and positioning against single-step reconstruction and gradient-based refinement remain.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the narrative remain intact. Local passages are rewritten, training details move to Appendix B, and the appendix gains separate evaluation, visualization, and LLM-use sections. The acknowledgments are removed; the expansion primarily documents added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tables and plots, rebuilds Figure 3 with rendering-error heatmaps and per-image PSNR, adds a view-count generalization panel, and introduces iteration and ablation visualizations. Existing compression and Gaussian-reconstruction images are retained and relocated: v1 Figures 6-8 become v2 Figures 7, 12, and 13.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in evidence for recurrent refinement: Table 8 controls initialization, while Table 9 compares weight sharing against stacked and deeper alternatives. Expanded mechanism ablations and generalization tests substantially strengthen support for the central contribution. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems, including Table 8's 0.960 SSIM entry conflicting with its best-value highlighting and the removed timing-hardware disclosure.
